title: DR1 asks for the means of transport with a dropdown; the frontend asks with four radios.

finding.frontend: Under the legend "Means of transport to the port of entry" the four options are laid out as radios, all visible without opening anything: Airplane, Railway, Road Vehicle, Vessel (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:29-39).
finding.prototype: The same four options sit in a select that opens on "Select one" (app/views/arrival-details.html:110-120). The labels and their order are identical to the frontend's.
finding.difference: Nothing about the question, the options or their wording differs — only the control. Replace the four radios with a select that opens on "Select one", keeping the four labels and their order. Worth flagging to the designer when the work is picked up: a four-option question sits inside the range where the GOV.UK Design System asks for radios, and DR1 uses radios for every other short option set in the service, so the select on this one field may be an oversight in the signed-off design rather than an intention. That is a question about DR1, not about whether the frontend currently matches it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding radios rather than a select behind "Means of transport to the port of entry" in DR1 — its rendered DOM for that field is a single govuk-select with five options.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and both full-page screenshots for fe-arrival-details and dr1-arrival-details, and opened both cited sources at the cited lines. Ran the falsifier: DR1's captured DOM holds <select class="govuk-select app-arrival-form__means-select" id="means-of-transport" name="meansOfTransport"> with five options ("Select one", Airplane, Railway, Road Vehicle, Vessel), so it does not fire; the frontend's is a govukRadios block with the same four values. Citations are exact — port-of-entry.njk:29-39 is the govukRadios block and arrival-details.html:110-120 is the govukSelect block. Every factual claim CORRECT. Rubric 7 does not fire and the band was wrong: DR1 does not contradict itself here, and the author's stated settling condition ("a designer confirming whether the select on this one field was deliberate") is a question about whether the change is wanted, which this corpus settles in advance. Rebanded disputed to frontend-work and rewrote finding.difference as the work; see correction.
finding.correction: Claimed: band `disputed`, on the grounds that "changing the frontend to match would move a four-option question out of the pattern the GOV.UK Design System asks for" and that the answer might be "to correct DR1 and close this, not to change the frontend". True: DR1 is signed off, the difference is observed on both sides, and nothing about the finding's correctness is in doubt — so by the band table this is `frontend-work`, and the Design System argument is a desirability argument, which is out of scope on this corpus. Checked by reading the band table in FINDING-CONTRACT.md against the evidence: `disputed` is for a finding whose own correctness is in doubt or where DR1 contradicts itself, and neither holds — DR1 uses a select on this field consistently and says nothing anywhere that a select here would violate. The GDS-pattern observation is kept in finding.difference as a flag for whoever picks the work up, not as a block.
